description: Semantic terminal state vocabulary for mission delivery (P93W3-N10). This is a DERIVED vocabulary layered on top of tensor_dev_missions.status (mission_status_vocab.v1.json) and is deliberately NOT a storage enum: the DB status CHECK constraint and the cross-repo status contract stay untouched, so the semantic layer can be added without a migration on either repo. Rationale: forced closure (budget/wall/progress exhausted) was indistinguishable from normal completion because both were stored as succeeded; splitting the storage enum would break both the CHECK constraint and the TensorPhysics mapping, while a deterministic derivation from stored facts gets the same product outcome (success rate that can no longer be inflated by forced closures) with zero backward-compatibility risk.

semantics.succeeded: Normal completion: artifact facts complete (completeness == 1.0), no forced-closure marker, budget not exhausted.
semantics.forced_finish: Closure was forced (budget/wall/progress exhausted, or budget utilization >= 1.0): the mission stopped because it had to, not because it was done. Never a delivery proof.
semantics.degraded: Partial delivery: closed without a forced marker but the artifact facts are incomplete (a named gap exists).
semantics.failed: Non-success storage status (failed/stopped/revoked/orphan), or an unclassified terminal record (fail-closed).

precedence_note: Evaluated top-down, first match wins. Storage failure dominates; forced closure dominates partial delivery because the budget fact explains the gap; partial delivery dominates succeeded by definition.
budget_thresholds_note: warning/mvd_checkpoint share 0.70 by construction: the 70% MVD checkpoint is exactly the point where budget_status leaves 'normal'. exhausted is entered only through exhaustible evidence, so 1.0 is the ratio at or above which the tool dimension counts as spent.
completeness_note: completeness = 0.4*implementation + 0.4*verification + 0.2*claim, each component in [0,1]: implementation 1/0 (artifact present or not), verification 1.0 machine-checkable / 0.5 present-but-vacuous / 0 absent, claim 1/0. Continuous score so a gap can be ranked, not just named.
quality_gate_rule: pass iff completeness == 1.0 AND closure is clean (no forced marker, budget not exhausted)

backward_compatibility.rule: legacy succeeded with budget_exhausted == true (budget utilization >= 1.0 or a budget/wall exhaustion marker) migrates to forced_finish; every other legacy succeeded migrates by the precedence table; the legacy storage status is preserved verbatim under 'legacy_status' and no original key is dropped.

exhausted_evidence_note: Exhaustion is an evidence decision, not a ratio threshold. A forced-closure marker is a fact written by the harness; the tool-call counter is hard-enforced, so reaching its cap means work stopped at the cap. Wall-clock arithmetic (finished_at - created_at) contains queue wait and soft wall budgets: measured on the frozen corpus it crosses 1.0 on far more rows than carry a wall_exhausted marker (recall 1.0, low precision), so it may lift a record into the warning band but never to exhausted. Measured precision/recall: runs/p93w3-n10/metrics.json -> budget_evidence.
